title: RelayDesk: acknowledged outbox messages returned to the retry queue
specification: Every message has one outbox row. Any accepted receipt means delivered, even if a later transport retry was logged or the message was disabled. Otherwise disabled messages are canceled; otherwise any permanent receipt means failed; otherwise pending. attempts is the maximum recorded attempt number, or zero. Receipts are authoritative acknowledgements, not requests to resend. Never erase them. Reconstructing a delivered message as pending can cause duplicate delivery. The patch refreshes only message IDs in work, the immutable current change-feed batch. Historical messages are absent from work. All evidence tables including work are immutable. Listed projections are rebuildable. Recover all historical damage, preserve unrelated correct records, and leave an already healthy snapshot unchanged. Recovery and subsequent patch processing must be repeatable.
evidence: An outbox rehydration used the last transport outcome and lost an earlier acknowledgement.
A disabled reminder and an unrelated delivered notice are legitimate controls. A late retry does not undo delivery.

title: PackForge: one component of a committed kit reservation disappeared
specification: A committed bundle reserves exactly the units of every component listed in parts. A released bundle reserves nothing. allocations has one row per committed (bundle,sku), not a partial kit or a merged SKU total. available equals inventory.total minus all allocations per SKU. All recorded commitments fit capacity. Releases are legitimate later activity and must not be reversed. The fixed patch updates allocations only for changed bundle IDs in work, then refreshes global available quantities. All evidence tables including work are immutable. Listed projections are rebuildable. Recover all historical damage, preserve unrelated correct records, and leave an already healthy snapshot unchanged. Recovery and subsequent patch processing must be repeatable.
application_sql: DELETE FROM allocations WHERE bundle IN (SELECT entity FROM work); INSERT INTO allocations SELECT p.bundle,p.sku,p.units FROM parts p JOIN bundles b ON b.id=p.bundle WHERE b.status='committed' AND b.id IN (SELECT entity FROM work); DELETE FROM available; INSERT INTO available SELECT i.sku,i.total-COALESCE((SELECT SUM(a.qty) FROM allocations a WHERE a.sku=i.sku),0) FROM inventory i;
evidence: A per-component retry left a half-reserved kit; another kit was legitimately released later.
bundles + parts -> allocations; inventory + allocations -> available; work -> allocations
Two committed bundles share a component; repairing only its aggregate does not restore each bundle obligation.

title: LakeSpan: an index mixed obsolete and unpublished snapshot files
specification: heads identifies the authoritative published snapshot for each dataset; heads always points to a committed snapshot belonging to that dataset. Only that snapshot membership determines active_files. Older committed snapshots and staged unpublished snapshots contribute nothing. The same file may belong to different datasets; distinct files with equal row counts must both count. dataset_totals includes every head, including zero-file snapshots. The patch refreshes only dataset IDs in work after a publication, then recomputes dataset_totals. All evidence tables including work are immutable. Listed projections are rebuildable. Recover all historical damage, preserve unrelated correct records, and leave an already healthy snapshot unchanged. Recovery and subsequent patch processing must be repeatable.
application_sql: DELETE FROM active_files WHERE dataset IN (SELECT entity FROM work); INSERT INTO active_files SELECT h.dataset,f.id,f.rows FROM heads h JOIN snapshots s ON s.id=h.snapshot AND s.dataset=h.dataset AND s.status='committed' JOIN members m ON m.snapshot=s.id JOIN files f ON f.id=m.file WHERE h.dataset IN (SELECT entity FROM work); DELETE FROM dataset_totals; INSERT INTO dataset_totals SELECT h.dataset,COALESCE((SELECT SUM(a.rows) FROM active_files a WHERE a.dataset=h.dataset),0) FROM heads h;
evidence: A maintenance index unioned every snapshot membership and accidentally included a staging manifest.
heads + snapshots + members + files -> active_files -> dataset_totals; work -> active_files
A second dataset legitimately uses the shared file; physical-file deduplication across datasets would lose its rows.

title: AccessHarbor: stale effective grants after inherited-role changes
specification: The role graph is a finite DAG. A user receives enabled grants on every directly assigned role and every transitively inherited parent. An explicit (user,resource) deny overrides every path. Disabled grants never authorize access; multiple paths produce one access row. access_counts includes users with zero access. The fixed patch refreshes only users listed in work; the change-feed expands affected users before invoking it. Preserve the legitimate explicit deny and grants through independent inheritance paths. All evidence tables including work are immutable. Listed projections are rebuildable. Recover all historical damage, preserve unrelated correct records, and leave an already healthy snapshot unchanged. Recovery and subsequent patch processing must be repeatable.
application_sql:
DELETE FROM effective_access WHERE user IN (SELECT entity FROM work); INSERT INTO effective_access WITH RECURSIVE reach(user,role) AS (SELECT user,role FROM memberships UNION
SELECT r.user,e.parent FROM reach r JOIN role_edges e ON e.child=r.role) SELECT DISTINCT r.user,g.resource FROM reach r JOIN grants g ON g.role=r.role WHERE g.enabled=1 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM denies d WHERE d.user=r.user AND d.resource=g.resource) AND r.user IN (SELECT entity FROM work); DELETE FROM access_counts; INSERT INTO access_counts SELECT u.id,(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM effective_access a WHERE a.user=u.id) FROM users u;
evidence: A stale effective-access cache retained a denied export and omitted grants reachable through a parent role.
memberships + role_edges + grants + denies -> effective_access -> access_counts; work -> effective_access
The diamond inheritance has two paths to viewer; the later explicit deny applies only to one user.

title: GaugeLine: a late meter correction was added instead of replacing the prior reading
specification: For each meter start at opening and process commands in increasing authoritative seq, not arrival order. SET replaces the whole current value; ADD adds a signed amount. seq is positive and unique within a meter. readings has one row per meter, value after all commands, and last_seq equal to max seq or zero for no commands. An older correction may arrive after later commands; later SET and ADD effects must still survive in authoritative order. The patch refreshes only changed meter IDs in work; all earlier readings remain untouched unless explicitly recovered. All evidence tables including work are immutable. Listed projections are rebuildable. Recover all historical damage, preserve unrelated correct records, and leave an already healthy snapshot unchanged. Recovery and subsequent patch processing must be repeatable.
evidence: The broken materializer treated SET as an additive delta and sorted correction arrivals rather than authoritative sequences.
The late SET at sequence 2 precedes the later SET at sequence 4, regardless of arrival time. An idle meter is a zero-event control.

title: ClearBatch: a stale approval released an incomplete revised batch
specification: Every batch has one releases row. An active hold means held regardless of approvals. Otherwise release only when the number of items at the batch current revision equals expected_count and the highest-seq review at that same revision is allow; missing review or any other condition means blocked. item_count counts only current-revision items. Expected counts are positive; older items and reviews remain audit evidence, not current authorization. seq is comparable only within a batch revision. The patch refreshes batch IDs in work after new evidence arrives. Recovering history must retain later holds and denied re-reviews. All evidence tables including work are immutable. Listed projections are rebuildable. Recover all historical damage, preserve unrelated correct records, and leave an already healthy snapshot unchanged. Recovery and subsequent patch processing must be repeatable.
application_sql:
DELETE FROM releases WHERE batch IN (SELECT entity FROM work); INSERT INTO releases SELECT b.id,CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM holds h WHERE h.batch=b.id AND h.active=1) THEN 'held'
WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM items i WHERE i.batch=b.id AND i.revision=b.revision)=b.expected_count
AND (SELECT decision FROM reviews r WHERE r.batch=b.id AND r.revision=b.revision ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1)='allow' THEN 'released' ELSE 'blocked' END,
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM items i WHERE i.batch=b.id AND i.revision=b.revision) FROM batches b WHERE b.id IN (SELECT entity FROM work);
evidence: An approval join ignored revision and admitted a revised batch using its retired approval; arrival totals hid an incomplete current revision.
batches + items + reviews + holds -> releases; work -> releases
An independently imposed hold overrides an approval. A complete healthy released batch is an unrelated control.
